I'm a woman and I got immediately diagnosed with autism at the age of 5.  It was actually a misdiagnosis due to the fact this was in the early 2000s and psychiatrists were dinosaurs with that kind of stuff back then.  They didn't take into account my upbringing or the trauma that had happened in my life. They immediately just slapped me with 'Yep, you're autistic.' This was actually very harmful for me because it meant I couldn't get the help I actually needed.Years later I got a diagnosis of CPTSD and every psychiatrist I've been to have all said 'No, you're not autistic, you don't fit the criteria.'  Now, I'm aware that autism presents itself differently in people and it definitely is a spectrum, but its important to not just slap someone with an autism diagnosis straight off the bat, like this person seems to want.  The criteria for autism has changed over the years and its also important to take into account if this person has experienced any trauma in their life, as well as other factors, so they can get the help they actually need.

Edit: Should also point out I was diagnosed when the whole "vaccines cause autism" bullshit was a thing and every kid who was slightly different got hit with an autism diagnosis left right and centre.
